nodes.label: Game availability during highscore loading and saving
Running game to highscore recorder
nodes.untrusted_input: score, survival time, and player name produced or supplied by the running game

nodes.label: External game content
nodes.untrusted_input: content loaded from outside the program, including shared level data

nodes.failure_behavior: Reject and report the invalid input without substituting or clamping it.
nodes.label: The operation receiving a run result must accept only valid score, survival-time, and player-name values, reject and report invalid input, and never substitute or clamp values.
nodes.task_relevance: Protects the integrity of records at run completion.

nodes.failure_behavior: Use the stated defaults or normalized values and continue the recording operation.
nodes.label: The caller integrating run completion must normalize missing or invalid run values to stated safe defaults before invoking the recording operation, so recording still occurs.
nodes.task_relevance: Preserves the primary highscore effect when game state is incomplete or malformed.

nodes.failure_behavior: Reject and report malformed or unsupported file data without deserializing objects.
nodes.label: The highscore store must treat the local file as untrusted data, parse it without Java object deserialization, and reject malformed records while reporting the rejection.
nodes.task_relevance: Prevents crafted local files from altering parser behavior or executing code.

nodes.failure_behavior: Reject and report data exceeding any configured limit.
nodes.label: Reads of the highscore file must enforce limits on file size, record count, field lengths, and numeric ranges before retaining or displaying data.
nodes.task_relevance: Bounds resource use from a user-editable persistence file.

nodes.failure_behavior: Reject and report an insertion that violates collection bounds rather than growing without limit.
nodes.label: The highscore collection must retain no more than a configured maximum number of records and must sort retained names by validated points in descending order.
nodes.task_relevance: Keeps displayed and persisted highscore data bounded and consistent.

nodes.failure_behavior: Report the persistence failure and continue with the stated safe in-memory default.
nodes.label: Malformed or unavailable highscore data must not prevent the game or menu from running; the caller must use an empty or otherwise stated safe in-memory board before continuing the display or recording effect.
nodes.task_relevance: Maintains game availability when persistence is damaged.

nodes.failure_behavior: The receiving operation rejects and reports the invalid input.
nodes.label: A strict validation routine at the receiving recording and parsing operations rejects invalid values and emits an actionable error result or diagnostic.

nodes.failure_behavior: The caller substitutes the stated defaults and calls the recording operation.
nodes.label: A run-end integration adapter normalizes missing or invalid score, time, and name values to explicit safe defaults before calling the recorder.

nodes.failure_behavior: The reader rejects and reports malformed, oversized, or overlong input.
nodes.label: A bounded streaming or size-limited reader parses a simple data format and excludes Java object deserialization.

nodes.failure_behavior: The collection rejects and reports entries beyond its configured bound.
nodes.label: A bounded collection enforces a maximum retained record count and orders validated records by descending score.

nodes.failure_behavior: The caller reports the failure, substitutes an empty board, and continues the primary feature effect.
nodes.label: A persistence failure boundary catches parse, I/O, and validation failures and initializes a safe empty board before menu display or run recording continues.

summary: Security context for a Java desktop game's local highscore persistence and menu display.
